title: Ingress Observability Bakeoff and Telemetry Declaration for Enterprise Cutovers
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the standardized bakeoff and telemetry declaration process used during enterprise tenant cutovers and large customer integrations. The goal is to validate ingress observability, telemetry completeness, and SLA readiness before a production flip. This reduces incident churn, shortens the stabilization window, and provides a clear pass/fail decision path for the cutover gate.

Scope: Applies to Dedicated and Private launch cutovers and any Hosted onboarding with >1M monthly tokens or complex network topologies (VPC peering, private link, or regional egress controls). Not intended for small self-serve trials.

Audience: Customer Success Engineers, Solutions Engineers, Platform Oncall, Customer SRE, and Product Integration owners.

Summary of changes vs. previous practice:
- Formalizes a measurable bakeoff with explicit SLO thresholds and telemetry schema declaration.
- Introduces a compact "Telemetry Declaration" template that customers and Redwood must sign off on before canary.
- Defines ownership and escalation paths for failed observability checks to prevent ambiguous handoffs.

Roles & Responsibilities

- Customer Success (CSE): coordinates schedule, invites stakeholders, captures acceptance artifact.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): runs ingress tests, verifies request/response parity and header-level telemetry.
- Customer SRE / Network: validates network routing, TLS, and client certificate behavior.
- Platform Oncall: validates server-side traces, span naming, and alerts.
- Product Integration Owner: final sign-off for functional equivalence and rollout readiness.

Pre-bakeoff checklist (minimum required)

1) Provisioning and access
- Tenant configuration deployed (route table, DNS entries, certs, API keys).
- Red-team access account for SE & Platform Oncall active.
- Signed Telemetry Declaration draft (see template).

2) Baseline telemetry verified
- Metrics exposed: ingress_rps, ingress_error_rate, request_latency_p50/p95, token_count_per_request.
- Traces created for request start/end and model invocation with parent/child spans.
- Logs include request_id, tenant_id, route, and sampling flag.

3) Alerting and dashboards
- Canary dashboard created with the tenant tag.
- Alerts configured: ErrorRate >= 2% sustained for 5m, p95 latency > 2s for 10m, Token cost delta +30% vs baseline for 1h (optional).

Bakeoff procedure (90–120 minute window recommended)

Preparation (30m)
1. Confirm windows and invites; ensure stakeholders available for rapid decisions.
2. Seed simulated workload: run the standard ingress load generator for the workload class (examples in appendix).
3. Snapshot baseline: capture current dashboards, traces, and logs as the "pre-bakeoff" reference.

Phase A — Functional validation (20m)
1. Run 200–500 requests across core routes with representative payloads (short, medium, long).
2. Verify request/response parity for 100% of sampled requests (no silent truncation, correct streaming delim).
3. Validate header propagation: X-Request-Id, X-Tenant-Id, X-Region, X-Trace-Parent.
4. Record sample traces (3 successful, 1 with synthetic error) and attach to the bakeoff notes.

Phase B — Observability validation (30m)
1. Metrics: Confirm ingestion to Redwood telemetry or customer telemetry endpoint within 60s for meter points below.
2. Traces: Open a trace in APM and confirm model invocation spans contain span attributes: model.name, model.version, kv_cache_hit (true|false), quantized (true|false).
3. Logs: Search last 500 log lines for request_id mapping to trace_id.
4. Dashboard: Canary dashboard shows ingresses tagged by tenant and route.

Phase C — Stress and edge-cases (20–40m)
1. Burst test: 3x expected peak RPS for 60s to validate aggregation and sampling behavior.
2. Partial failure: Induce an artificial model timeout for 30s and confirm fallback policy is visible in traces and fallback_count metric increases.
3. Token and billing sample: Send a mixture of short/long prompts and compare per-request token metadata to billing token counters.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail)

Pass requires ALL of the following: (explicit numeric thresholds)
- End-to-end request success rate >= 98% during functional validation.
- Observability latency: metrics ingestion lag <= 60s 95% of the time.
- Traces sampled and linkable: >= 95% of sampled request IDs must map to at least one trace with a model invocation span.
- Header propagation: 100% of sampled requests must contain X-Request-Id and X-Tenant-Id in both logs and inbound request headers.
- Alerts: No unacknowledged critical alerts fired during the bakeoff window (SRE may temporarily mute non-actionable alerts with approval).

Fail conditions (examples)
- Metrics ingestion lag > 120s or >5% metric points lost.
- Traces missing model invocation attributes in >=10% of sampled traces.
- Token accounting divergence >15% vs expected (requires immediate triage).

Telemetry Declaration Template (customer + Redwood sign-off)

Provide the following fields and confirm agreement before canary. Use the minimal JSON snippet below as the canonical declaration that will be attached to the cutover ticket.

--- JSON snippet (single-line friendly) ---
{ "tenant_id": "<tenant-id>", "telemetry_target": "redwood:observability-prod OR customer:apm-endpoint", "metrics": ["ingress_rps","ingress_error_rate","request_latency_p95","token_count_per_request"], "traces_required": true, "log_fields_required": ["request_id","tenant_id","route","status_code"], "ingestion_slo_seconds": 60 }

Notes on fields:
- telemetry_target: specify if telemetry should be forwarded to Redwood ingestion or to a customer-managed APM. If customer-managed, include endpoint and auth in related secure doc.
- traces_required: if false, bakeoff must be approved only for low-risk features; default is true.

Telemetry mapping recommendations

Metric name -> Redwood canonical mapping
- ingress_rps -> telemetry.ingress.rps
- ingress_error_rate -> telemetry.ingress.errors.percentage
- request_latency_p95 -> telemetry.ingress.latency.p95_ms
- token_count_per_request -> telemetry.billing.tokens_per_req

Span attribute recommendations
- model.name (string)
- model.version (string)
- model.invocation_time_ms (number)
- kv_cache_hit (boolean)
- quantized (boolean)
- request.priority (string)

Rollout decision matrix (example)

- Green: All acceptance criteria met -> Proceed to canary (10% traffic) and schedule 2-hour monitoring block.
- Yellow: One non-critical observability gap (e.g., missing optional span attribute) -> Defer canary until quick remediation or allow canary under compensating control (shorter canary, increased sampling). Must be approved by Platform Oncall and CSE.
- Red: Any metric or trace lag failures, token accounting divergence >15%, or missing header propagation -> Halt cutover and open a joint incident with SRE and SE.

Post-bakeoff artifacts (deliverable attachments)

- Bakeoff summary note (1–2 pages).
- Exported sample traces (3–10 traces) with trace IDs.
- Canary dashboard snapshot (PNG).
- Signed Telemetry Declaration JSON (attached to ticket).

Escalation & contact matrix

- First 15m: On-call Platform Engineer (pager) + SE lead slack channel (#se-platform-integration).
- 15–60m: Customer SRE + CSE primary.
- >60m or critical failure: Engineering Incident Lead and Product Integration Owner notified; declare joint incident with runbook id: OB-INGRESS-2028.

Appendix A — Example commands and snippets

Curl header propagation verification:

curl -s -D - -H "X-Request-Id: test-req-123" -H "X-Tenant-Id: tenant-prod-42" https://tenant.example.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq '.

Telemetry sampling rule (Prometheus-style pseudo):

# Record per-tenant p95 in ms
record: tenant_request_latency_p95_ms = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant=~"tenant-prod-.*"}[5m])) by (le, tenant))

APM query example (search traces for a request id):
trace_id = search_traces("attributes.request_id:test-req-123")

Appendix B — Workload generator reference

- Use the ingress-load-tool repo (internal): se-tools/ingress-load-generator. Recommended profile: "enterprise-chat-mixed" (50% short, 30% medium, 20% long).
- Command: ./loadgen --profile enterprise-chat-mixed --tenants tenant-prod-42 --rps 50 --duration 300

Governance and versioning

This document is the canonical bakeoff procedure for enterprise ingress observability. Any deviations must be recorded on the cutover ticket and approved by Customer Success and Platform Oncall. Changes to the Telemetry Declaration template must be reviewed by the Observability Standards working group.
